channel.title: FXStreet Forex & Commodities News
channel.description: Real-time Forex News and the latest trading updates. Stay updated on the latest news about currencies and commodities markets.

item.title: Silver Price Forecast: Can bulls defend $60 as the US Dollar climbs to one-year highs?
item.description: Silver (XAG/USD) slides more than 4% on Tuesday as the US Dollar (USD) climbs to near one-year highs after the Federal Reserve's (Fed) hawkish tilt at last week's monetary policy meeting reinforced expectations that interest rates will remain higher for longer.

item.title: Euro: Eurozone PMIs show two-speed recovery – TD Securities
item.description: TD Securities’ Global Strategy Team reports that June Eurozone PMIs confirm a divergence between stabilizing German manufacturing and still weak French services.

item.title: US S&P Global PMI expected to highlight resilient business activity in June
item.description: S&P Global will release the June flash Purchasing Managers' Indices (PMIs) for most major economies, with the United States (US) data scheduled on Tuesday. These surveys of top private-sector executives are seen as an early indicator of the country’s economic health.

item.title: Fed: Warsh era keeps markets guessing – NBC
item.description: National Bank of Canada (NBC) Economics and Strategy team, led by Taylor Schleich, Ethan Currie and Vy Le, argues that Kevin Warsh’s Federal Reserve (Fed) is deliberately increasing policy ambiguity by stripping out forward guidance.

item.title: Euro: Softer PMIs challenge ECB tightening case – BNY
item.description: Geoff Yu at BNY highlights that Eurozone PMIs remain weak despite a slightly better-than-expected composite reading. Core economies like Germany and France continue to underperform, with German services at a 43‑month low.

item.title: Natural gas: Heat and outages support prices – Commerzbank
item.description: Commerzbank analysts highlight that stronger heatwaves in Europe and Asia are likely to lift electricity demand and gas-fired power use, complicating European storage refilling.

item.title: US Dollar Index: Breakout risks build on hawkish Fed – OCBC
item.description: OCBC’s Sim Moh Siong notes the Dollar is supported by higher US Treasury yields and a more hawkish Federal Reserve path, with leaner Fed communication likely to lift FX volatility.

item.title: United States ADP Employment Change 4-week average increases to 30.75K
item.description: Private-sector hiring in the US has increased in early June. According to the NER Pulse, the weekly companion to the ADP National Employment Report, companies added an average of 30.75K jobs per week in the four weeks ending June 6.

item.title: $4,000: Major level comes into focus as stronger US Dollar weighs on Gold
item.description: Gold (XAU/USD) trades on the back foot on Monday, pressured by a stronger US Dollar (USD) and rising expectations that the Federal Reserve (Fed) could raise interest rates later this year.

item.title: Oil: Softer path for Brent and WTI as Hormuz reopens – Rabobank
item.description: Rabobank’s energy strategists Joe DeLaura and Florence Schmit cuts Brent and WTI (West Texas Intermediate) forecasts after the Versailles MoU (Memorandum of Understanding) and gradual reopening of the Strait of Hormuz.

item.title: Australian Dollar: Softer CPI keeps RBA sidelined – TD Securities
item.description: TD Securities’ Global Strategy Team expects Australian headline Consumer Price Index (CPI) to ease to 4.2% year-on-year in May, helped by lower transport and recreational prices.

item.title: EUR/USD Price Forecast: Testing 11-month lows at 1.3991 amid broad US Dollar strength
item.description: The Euro (EUR) extends losses on Tuesday, with the US Dollar (USD) buoyed by rising hopes of Federal Reserve (Fed) tightening later this year and a cautious market mood, amid the uncertainty surrounding the US-Iran trade deal.

item.title: Japanese Yen: Intervention risk rises with 40-year low against USD – BNY
item.description: BNY’s Geoff Yu highlights rising Japanese Yen intervention risk after Finance Minister Satsuki Katayama’s call with U.S. Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent. Japan and the U.S. reaffirmed a shared stance that bold FX action remains possible, even as Katayama avoided commenting on current levels.

item.title: Australian Dollar hits hard by risk-aversion mood, Aussie CPI data awaited
item.description: The Australian Dollar (AUD) underperforms its currency peers, trading 0.8% lower at around 0.6945 against the US Dollar (USD) during the European session on Tuesday.

item.title: Gold: Greenspan legacy and central bank demand – Commerzbank
item.description: Commerzbank’s Carsten Fritsch uses Alan Greenspan’s death to revisit his long-standing support for Gold as a premier currency.

item.title: US President Trump: Iran agreed to highest level nuclear inspections long into future
item.description: In a post published on Truth Social on Tuesday, United States (US) President Donald Trump claimed that Iran has "fully and completely" agreed to highest level nuclear inspections long into the future.

item.title: Aluminium: Deficit persists despite higher output – ING
item.description: ING strategists Warren Patterson and Ewa Manthey say global Aluminium output is rising, including in China, Europe and Asia ex-China, but the market remains in deficit. They estimate around 3mt of capacity has been lost to Middle East disruptions and is unlikely to return quickly.

item.title: Hungarian Forint: HUF strength supports easing path – Societe Generale
item.description: Societe Generale analysts expect the Hungarian central bank Magyar Nemzeti Bank (MNB) to cut rates by 25 bps to 6.0%, citing improved sentiment after Peter Magyar’s election victory and an EU-friendly policy stance.

item.title: Indian Rupee weakens against US Dollar amid Fed interest rate hike bets
item.description: The Indian Rupee (INR) trades lower against the US Dollar (USD) on Tuesday.

item.title: Gold Price Forecast: XAU/USD hovers above $4,100 amid growing bearish pressure
item.description: Gold (XAU/USD) reversed Monday’s gains and resumed the broader bearish trend on Tuesday, testing support at the $4,100 level after failing to extend gains beyond $4,220 on Monday.

item.title: New Zealand Dollar slumps amid hawkish Fed bets, eyes on US PMI data
item.description: The New Zealand Dollar (NZD) faces significant selling pressure against its major currency peers during the European session on Tuesday, trading 0.4% lower at around 0.5690. The pair is under pressure as hawkish Federal Reserve (Fed) bets have weakened the appeal of riskier assets.

item.title: GBP/JPY Price Forecasts: Pound retreats to 213.20, lacking a clear bias
item.description: The British Pound (GBP) pares Monday’s gains against the Japanese Yen (JPY) on Tuesday, weighed down by higher intervention risks and downbeat UK business activity figures.

item.title: Canadian Dollar: BoC patience persists with firmer CPI – TD Securities
item.description: TD Securities strategists note that Canadian headline Consumer Price Index (CPI) for May surprised to the upside, driven by energy and seasonal factors, while core measures remained stable near 2%.

item.title: Iran signals no early nuclear talks as it rules out missile negotiations
item.description: Iran reaffirmed its red line on military issues on Tuesday, as markets continue to monitor geopolitical developments in the Middle East.

item.title: Euro: Inflation scare questioned as 1.13 level eyed – Societe Generale
item.description: Societe Generale’s Kenneth Broux and colleagues highlight softer Eurozone PMI price data and a dovish tone from European Central Bank (ECB) President Lagarde as key drivers for EUR/USD. They see the 1.13-handle as in focus, with support around 1.1390 and 1.1350.

item.title: Japanese Yen edges up from long-term lows amid higher intervention risks
item.description: The Japanese Yen (JPY) is picking up against the US Dollar (USD) on Tuesday after hitting lows a few pips above the 40-year low of 161.95 on Monday.

item.title: Silver price today: Silver falls, according to FXStreet data
item.description: Silver prices (XAG/USD) fell on Tuesday, according to FXStreet data. Silver trades at $62.18 per troy ounce, down 4.47% from the $65.09 it cost on Monday.

item.title: Fed: Warsh era brings quieter guidance – BNY
item.description: BNY’s John Velis and David Tam argue that Chair Kevin Warsh is steering Federal Reserve communications toward less forward guidance and a stronger emphasis on price stability.

item.title: Indian Rupee: Support from flows and policy backdrop – DBS
item.description: DBS Group Research economist Radhika Rao notes that India’s 10Y government bond yield has remained confined between 6.90% and 7.05% as domestic and global drivers offset each other.

item.title: British Pound sticks to intraday losses vs bullish USD after downbeat UK PMIs
item.description: The GBP/USD pair adds to its modest intraday losses and touches a fresh daily low, around the 1.3215-1.3210 region during the first half of the European session.
